alalal-c47736-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 18: whether being in place and being local are the same, and how they apply to God, created spirit and body.

alalal-c47736-d1e120.summary: Raises the doubt whether being in place is the same as being local.

alalal-c47736-d1e127.summary: First argument for identity: being local consists only in the relation of place to the located, which is what 'being in place' implies.

alalal-c47736-d1e141.summary: Second argument: being in time is being temporal, so being in place, an external measuring quantity, is being local.

alalal-c47736-d1e152.summary: Further: being in time is being measured by a part of time (the Philosopher), so being in place is being measured by place, and whatever is measured by place is local.

alalal-c47736-d1e168.summary: Third argument: place is an accident and denominates its subject, the located, and 'local' expresses that denomination, so being in place and being local are the same.

alalal-c47736-d1e188.summary: Fourth argument: whatever is in place is located in place, and whatever is located is local, so whatever is in place is local. Against all this stands Lombard's text: God is in place but not local.

alalal-c47736-d1e212.summary: Solution: they differ, since being in place belongs to God, created spirit and body by priority and posteriority and equivocally. Taken from the properties of place, God is in place by giving it being and containing power, a created spirit by being in one place and not another, and a body per se with beginning, middle and end. Taken from the properties of the located, God is in place only metaphorically, filling it spiritually without distance or distinction, by not failing to give being and power. Being local, per Anselm, is following the laws of place: being bounded and contained from outside, which created spirits and bodies follow, and being circumscribed part for part, which only bodies follow.
claims: Being in place is said equivocally and by priority of God, created spirits and bodies.
Being local means following the laws of place, which apply in part to created spirits and fully only to bodies, and not at all to God.

alalal-c47736-d1e306.summary: Reply to the first argument: the laws of locality arise from the relation of place to located, but this relation is not the same for everything in place. Not everything in place is located; properly only a body is located, while a created spirit is in place definitively and is local only in a qualified sense.
claims: Only bodies are properly located; created spirits are in place definitively.

alalal-c47736-d1e340.summary: Reply to the second argument: being in time is not always being temporal, since things are in time in many ways, as the now, as parts, or as passions; being in time as in a measure is temporal, and likewise being in place as in a measure is local, but not every way of being in place is.

alalal-c47736-d1e373.summary: Reply to the third argument: place is an accident existing not in the located but in the locating body, being the surface of the surrounding body; and even if it denominated the located, being in place and being located are not the same.
claims: Place is an accident of the surrounding body, not of the located.

alalal-c47736-d1e397.summary: Reply to the fourth argument: 'whatever is in place is located in place' is false unless it concerns what is in place primarily and per se.

alalal-c47736.summary: Article 18 asks whether being in place and being local are the same, and how each applies to God, created spirits and bodies. Arguments for identity rely on the relation of place to located, on the analogy with being in time, and on place as an accident denominating the located. Albert distinguishes them. Being in place is said by priority and equivocally: God is in place by giving it being and containing power, and fills it only metaphorically; a created spirit is in place definitively; a body is in place per se. Being local, following Anselm, means following the laws of place. Bodies and spirits follow the law of being bounded and contained, but only bodies follow the law of circumscription part for part. Only bodies are properly located, and place is an accident of the surrounding body, not of the located.
claims: Being in place and being local are not the same.
God, created spirits and bodies are in place in analogically ordered, equivocal senses.
Only bodies are properly local and circumscribed; created spirits are in place definitively; God is not local at all.
concepts: esse in loco vs esse locale
